scope: Direct all-operator derivation of 121's one-site spin-flip, nonnegative erasure, negative-shrink mirror and fixed-Q pairing; no new input class, executable verification or independent review.
local_identity: For a general 2x2 complex matrix X=[[a,b],[c,d]], Y X^T Y=[[d,-b],[-c,a]]=Tr(X)I-X. Thus the linear spin-flip superoperator J_i=2E_i-Id, where E_i(X)=I_i tensor Tr_i(X)/2, holds on arbitrary operators, not only Hermitian densities. The J_i and E_i on distinct sites commute.
fixed_trace_erasure: For any four-qubit X, F(X)=4 sum_i E_i(X)-4X and full J(X)=X-2T1(X)+4T2(X)-8T3(X)+16T4(X). Since 8T3(X)=H1(X) and 16T4(X)=Tr(X)I, one obtains 4T2(X)=H1(X)+X+J(X)+F(X)/2-Tr(X)I. Therefore the input identity uses -I and a rank-three projector dual identity uses -3I. Both are actual matrix equalities with no transpose dropped.
negative_shrink_mirror: Let p'=2-p and t=p-1. At one site, Phi_p=t J+(1-t)E and J Phi_p'=J(t Id+(1-t)E)=t J+(1-t)E, using J E=E. Tensoring all four factors yields Lambda_p=J_global Lambda_p'. The global J is Y^tensor4 (full transpose) Y^tensor4, a positive trace-preserving spectrum-preserving map on Hermitian inputs. The product-reference spectra agree because a and b are swapped under p versus p'.
same_projector: For Hermitian Q and X, Tr[Q J_global(X)]=Tr[J_global(Q) X], using total trace-transpose symmetry. J_global maps every complex rank-three orthogonal projector bijectively to another such projector and preserves the trace. Thus the SAME actual rho and one deterministic transformed Q establish all negative-shrink fixed-Q comparisons; no independent optimizer, partial transpose, or nonlinear mixture argument is used.
